Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

guilty adjective

feeling guilty

also feel guilty, guilty conscience, bad conscience

classical

Plaut. Most. 544
Cic. Off. 3.73: sibi nūllīus culpae (Lewis & Short)

cōnscius, cōnscia, cōnscium

adjective; with sibi and the genitive of the fault

aware of a wrong one has done; guilty

With sibi, knowing something in oneself, for good or ill (Lewis & Short); by itself, guilty: animus cōnscius, a guilty conscience (Plaut. Most. 544).

Other words

  • cōnscientia, cōnscientiae f. — conscience; a guilty conscience

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 5.15: cōnscientia maleficiōrum (Lewis & Short)

    Also a good conscience: the guilt lies in the genitive or the context.

Examples

  • nihil est miserius quam animus hominis cōnscius

    nothing is more wretched than a man’s guilty consciencePlaut. Most. 544

See also guilty, I’m ashamed, I’m sorry, accept blame.

SourcesLewis & Short: conscius · Lewis & Short: conscientia
